tagline: Global Power Generation and Distribution Leader
hero_kpi_rationale: Capex reflects the strategic commitment to renewable energy and critical infrastructure, driving structural growth for the energy sector. 10% growth in 2025 despite an unfavorable macro environment, supported by deployments in clean energy and energy storage projects in the United States.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Amount invested annually in physical assets such as power plants or infrastructure.
kpis.description: Capex increased in 2025, driven by deployments in clean energy and energy storage projects in the United States.
kpis.signal: Increased investment in renewable projects despite macro headwinds.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenues and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin improved slightly due to better fixed cost management and the reclassification of Mong Duong as an operating asset.
kpis.signal: Improved operational efficiency in power generation activities.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating income divided by total revenues.
kpis.description: Operating margin declined due to foreign exchange contract losses and impairments related to non-viable renewable projects.
kpis.signal: Margin pressure from currency costs and write-downs of abandoned projects.

kpis.name: R&D Spending as Percentage of Revenue
kpis.explanation: Share of research and development expenses in total revenue.
kpis.description: R&D spending remains low but focused on improving solar and storage project efficiency.
kpis.signal: Modest R&D, concentrated on optimization of renewable projects.

kpis.name: Headcount (Employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: The company reduced headcount as part of an overall cost optimization following the sale of AES Brasil.
kpis.signal: Workforce reduction linked to the 2025 restructuring program.

kpis.name: General and Administrative Expenses
kpis.explanation: Costs related to central management and support functions.
kpis.description: G&A expenses decreased significantly in 2025 to $241M, driven by savings in IT costs ($18M), commercial development expenses ($34M), and professional fees ($8M), partially offset by $14M in one-time restructuring costs.
kpis.signal: Significant reduction due to restructuring and cost optimization.

kpis.name: Foreign Exchange Losses
kpis.explanation: Losses related to currency exchange rate fluctuations on international operations.
kpis.description: FX losses amounted to $79M in 2025, primarily driven by the depreciation of the Argentine peso and appreciation of the Chilean peso, with significant unrealized losses, notably in Argentina ($29M) and Chile ($50M). Currency derivative contracts recorded losses of $26M.
kpis.signal: Marked deterioration in Argentina and Chile due to depreciation of the Argentine peso and appreciation of the Chilean peso.

kpis.name: Asset Impairment Charges
kpis.explanation: Amount of write-downs for non-recoverable assets.
kpis.description: Impairment totaled $224M in 2025, down 40% from $374M in 2024. The decrease primarily reflects the reclassification of Mong Duong from 'held for sale' to 'held for use' (+$243M value reversal), partially offset by a $264M impairment charge at Maritza due to reduced expected cash flows following PPA contract expiration, and charges of $62M and $16M at AES Clean Energy Development and AES Andes, respectively, related to abandoned development projects.
kpis.signal: Sharp reduction due to Mong Duong reclassification and elimination of estimated selling costs.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale. Indicateur clé pour les investisseurs orientés revenus.
kpis.description: 5-year history of declared dividends per share (2021-2025).

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel du cash redistribué aux actionnaires : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions (treasury stock).
kpis.description: For 2025: cumulative dividends + share buybacks in billions USD.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du bénéfice net redistribuée en dividendes. Au-dessus de 80 % indique un dividende potentiellement non-soutenable.
kpis.description: Dividends / net income for 2025 (based on net income attributable to shareholders).

risks.title: Commodity Price Volatility
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in Item 1A with strong language on the potential impact of electricity, gas, and coal price fluctuations, particularly in certain markets (Chile, California). Exposure is partially hedged through contracts, but uncovered positions remain on certain short-term structures.

risks.title: Significant Foreign Exchange Risk
risks.score_rationale: Highlighted as a major risk in several countries (Argentina, Colombia, Eurozone). FX losses reached $79M in 2025 with uncovered exposure to the Argentine peso. The impact is already materialized with significant unrealized losses.

risks.title: Increased Competition from Renewables and Storage
risks.score_rationale: Repeatedly mentioned in several markets (Chile, California, Panama). The text indicates systemic downward pressure on electricity prices due to growing penetration of renewable energy and storage systems.

risks.title: Exposure to Weather and Hydrological Conditions
risks.score_rationale: Cited in Item 1A regarding hydroelectric assets in Colombia and Panama. Rainfall variations create spot market exposure when production deviates from contracted levels. The risk is recurring but partially managed through contracts.

risks.title: Variable Interest Rate Risk
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in the context of variable-rate debt. Total interest expense reached $1,407M in 2025. A portion is exposed to variable rates, although partially hedged via swaps.

risks.title: Dependence on Imperfectly Indexed Contracts
risks.score_rationale: Identified in several markets (California, Chile, Panama). Energy sales contracts do not fully adjust to cost fluctuations, leaving residual exposure, particularly evident at Maritza following PPA expiration.

risks.title: Dispatchability Risk in Panama
risks.score_rationale: Specific mention in Panama regarding new entrants potentially reducing dispatch availability for existing assets. The risk forces the purchase of expensive spot market power to fulfill PPAs.

ai_positioning.summary: AES does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
